name: The Role of Context

objectives.text: Tell what happened just before and just after a familiar event in a Bible story
Locate a verse in a Bible using its book, chapter, and verse numbers
Explain why we read the verses around a verse instead of choosing a verse at random
Identify who is speaking and who is being spoken to in a Bible passage
Summarize the paragraph surrounding a given verse in your own words
Explain how taking a verse out of its context can change what it seems to mean
Explain why a statement in Scripture must be read in light of its speaker, using the words of Job's friends as an example
Compare what the immediate context and the context of the whole book each show about the meaning of a verse
Use the surrounding verses to correct a common misreading of Philippians 4:13
Trace the logical flow of an argument in an epistle by following connecting words such as therefore, for, and but
Identify the stated purpose of a biblical book and use it to explain a passage within that book
Interpret a difficult verse by reading it within the argument of its whole chapter
Explain the three circles of context, immediate, book, and canonical, and how each one narrows the possible meaning of a verse
Explain why chapter and verse divisions are later additions and identify a passage whose thought continues across a chapter break
Analyze how Jesus answered Satan's misuse of a psalm by setting Scripture in its proper context
Construct a context chart for a biblical book showing its purpose, major sections, and the flow between them
Evaluate popular uses of isolated verses by comparing them with the meaning their contexts require
Defend the Reformed principle that a passage has one true sense which its context helps determine
Produce an exegetical outline of a passage that traces the author's line of thought from its context

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (before/after a story, locating a reference, summarizing the surrounding paragraph, out-of-context distortion, immediate vs book context, Philippians 4:13 correction, epistle argument flow, chapter-level interpretation, three circles, context chart, evaluating misreadings, defending the principle, exegetical outline). Dropped the generic beginning-middle-end item as general literacy that also leans toward genre. Recast 'pick verses like magic tricks' as an explanation grounded in Acts 17:11 and Nehemiah 8:8. Folded 'connect a passage to the book theme' into a sharper objective on a book's stated purpose (John 20:30-31, WLC Q157 'scope'). Added missing competencies: identifying speaker and audience, reading statements in light of the speaker (Job 42:7-8), chapter breaks as later additions, and Jesus' contextual answer to Satan's misuse of Psalm 91. Anchored the defense objective to WCF 1.9 on the single sense of Scripture and added further misreading examples (Jeremiah 29:11, Matthew 18:20, Matthew 7:1). Left authorial intent, genre, historical background, and Scripture-interprets-Scripture to sibling sub-topics.
